233: ✦Birth is approaching; you can start packing your hospital bag.✦But it's worth remembering that only about 5% of babies arrive on their due date.
234: ✦After birth, your baby will get all their nutrition from breast milk.✦So building healthy eating habits for breastfeeding is very important.✦Just as in pregnancy, your body will meet your baby's needs first.✦So eat healthily and carefully to meet both your needs.
235: ✦Another thing to watch while breastfeeding is how much you drink.✦Breastfeeding mothers are advised to drink about 2.7 litres of fluid a day.✦Tea, milk, juice and soup count toward this.✦Drinking plenty in the final weeks of pregnancy is also important.✦So now is the perfect time to build this habit.
236: ✦This is when mothers-to-be are at their most sensitive.✦In these weeks it can feel as if your tears have a mind of their own.✦This is the time when mothers cry the most.✦But it's due to the hormonal changes of pregnancy.✦Don't worry – it returns to normal after birth.
237: ✦Your baby is starting to behave like a newborn.✦The eyes are open when awake and closed when asleep.✦You may notice they've settled into sleep and wake periods.✦They've learned to blink.✦From this week your baby's breathing movements will increase.✦That's because your baby is preparing for real breathing after birth.
238: ✦The nails have grown to the fingertips.✦The skull bones are still quite soft and not fully joined.✦This will make it easier to pass through the narrow birth canal.✦At this stage, antibodies in your blood have started passing to your baby.✦The adrenal glands have developed and begun producing hormones that stimulate milk production.✦The vernix layer on the skin has thinned and the lanugo has almost completely gone.
239: ✦Tiredness is one of the most common complaints late in pregnancy.✦Sleeping comfortably gets harder.✦Avoiding daytime naps, eating dinner early, a warm bath and warm milk can help.✦Don't rely on caffeine to beat sleeplessness and fatigue; too much caffeine can affect the baby.✦And never take sleeping pills without your doctor's advice.
240: ✦You feel very tired and heavy – no surprise.✦Your uterus, once tucked away in your pelvis, now reaches up to your ribs.
241: ✦A fluid called colostrum is starting to leak from your breasts.✦It's the first milk your body makes for your baby, and it's packed with nutrients.✦You can use special pads made for breastfeeding mothers to absorb leaks inside your bra.
242: ✦You may have started having very vivid dreams.✦Dreams in pregnancy can be stranger than usual.✦These striking dreams reflect the changing feelings, emotions and thoughts of pregnancy.✦Changes in your body and life can bring fear or excitement.✦You might enjoy keeping a dream journal.
243: ✦Some dreams can be scary rather than magical.✦You may have realistic nightmares about the birth or your baby.✦Talking about your dreams with your partner or doctor will help.✦They'll confirm these dreams are normal.
244: ✦At this stage of pregnancy you may be prone to constipation.✦You can balance it by adding fibre to your meals.✦There are two types of fibre: soluble and insoluble.✦Soluble fibre dissolves in the intestines; the other passes through the digestive system undissolved.✦Increase your fibre intake slowly – it's gentler on your digestion.✦Drink plenty of fluids and do light exercise like yoga and walking.✦Some iron supplements can also cause constipation.✦Ask your doctor about this and about alternative supplements.
245: ✦Pain in your groin or vagina may be a sign that your cervix is starting to open.✦But this doesn't mean labour has started.✦Dilation can begin weeks before labour.
246: ✦At this stage you may have some contractions – or feel nothing at all.✦If you have cramps and feel your uterus tighten and harden, pay attention to how often and how regularly the contractions come.✦Tell your doctor how many minutes apart they are and how long they last.
247: ✦With your baby taking up so much room, sitting, standing and sleeping in normal positions is very hard.✦Small, frequent meals may help now.✦But don't worry – you'll feel relief when your baby drops lower into the pelvis.✦This is called engagement and usually happens a few weeks before birth.
248: ✦As your baby changes position, there's more pressure on your bladder.✦So you may need the toilet more often.✦But don't cut back on fluids because of it.✦Remember to drink more after physical activity too.
249: ✦Drink most of your daily fluids early in the day and less before bed.✦This way your sleep won't be interrupted as often.
250: ✦Your Braxton Hicks contractions may have increased.✦Go over the signs of labour with your doctor again and learn which symptoms mean you should call.✦Normally you don't need to call your doctor before your waters break or while contractions last less than a minute.✦But call your doctor if your baby moves less, you leak amniotic fluid, have vision problems, vaginal bleeding, a high fever, headache or abdominal pain.
251: ✦Go over the signs of labour with your doctor again and learn which symptoms mean you should call.✦Normally you don't need to call your doctor before your waters break or while contractions last less than a minute.✦But call your doctor if your baby moves less, you leak amniotic fluid, have vision problems, vaginal bleeding, a high fever, headache or abdominal pain.
252: ✦The human body is about 60% water and loses about 2 litres a day.✦This lost fluid must be replaced for healthy circulation and to clear waste.✦Drinking enough is also important for a healthy urinary tract and to prevent urinary infections.
253: ✦The normal, irregular contractions of your uterus may now be bothering you.✦You should be able to tell them apart from real labour pains.✦Your doctor will explain how to tell real labour from false labour.
254: ✦This week you're more comfortable in some ways.✦You may feel constantly hot and tired.✦That's because your body is working extra hard.✦The more blood your body circulates to nourish you and your baby, the more calories you burn.✦And this extra energy use raises your body temperature.
255: ✦If you find yourself cleaning like mad, your nesting instinct has kicked in.✦It's an instinct that prepares you for birth.✦Not every woman feels it, and it's harmless as long as you don't move heavy furniture.✦Never lift heavy things, because your ligaments are softened by pregnancy.✦So your risk of twisting an ankle or hurting your back is very high.✦Ask for help when you need it.
256: ✦If you want to clean, avoid harsh chemicals like bleach.✦If you have a cat, don't clean the litter box yourself, to avoid the risk of infection.✦Braxton Hicks contractions are now more frequent and stronger.
257: ✦Your vaginal discharge may have increased.✦If you see a small amount of blood in your underwear or in the toilet, labour may be only a few days away.✦If you have heavy bleeding, call your doctor immediately.
258: ✦Sleeping may feel harder than ever now.✦If possible, don't tire yourself out during the day.✦Keep tracking your baby's movements and call your doctor if you notice a decrease.
259: ✦With birth possible any day, if you're having a boy, you may want to think about whether you plan circumcision.✦Some parents prefer to have it done soon after birth.✦Talking to your doctor about it will help you decide.
260: ✦For most women the next few weeks are a waiting game.✦Use this time for your baby's room or jobs you won't have time for for a while after the birth.
261: ✦Your baby is almost here; you can pack your hospital bag now.✦Besides personal and practical items, it helps to bring nutritious snacks in case you need an energy boost during labour.✦You won't want to eat much, but a bite or two of something nutritious can help you keep going.✦Pack different foods; you won't know what you'll want or be able to tolerate until the time comes.
262: ✦You may find it harder and harder to sleep comfortably, especially at night.✦Rest often during the day and put your feet up. Nap, read and spend time with your partner while you can.
263: ✦Your baby is almost here; you can pack your hospital bag now.✦Besides personal and practical items, it helps to bring nutritious snacks in case you need an energy boost during labour.
264: ✦You won't want to eat much, but a bite or two of something nutritious can help you keep going.✦Pack different foods; you won't know what you'll want or be able to tolerate until the time comes.
265: ✦Don't forget to bring drinks so you don't get dehydrated.✦Some women find sports drinks handy, or you can bring water or juice in a sports bottle for easy sipping.
266: ✦From this week, keep in mind that labour could start at any moment.✦The key feature of real labour pains is that they come at regular intervals.✦They come on average 3 times in 10 minutes, each lasting about 50 seconds.✦They don't go away with rest and get stronger over time.✦Generally about 75% of births happen between weeks 38 and 42.✦In about 5% of mothers-to-be, labour doesn't start even after 42 weeks.✦The remaining 20% give birth before week 38.
267: ✦By 38 weeks most of the downy lanugo covering your baby's body has gone.✦The cheese-like vernix caseosa has mostly gone too (some may remain at birth).✦Your baby swallows both and keeps them in the intestines.✦They'll form the black stool passed in your baby's first bowel movements.✦This substance is called meconium.
268: ✦Here are the signs of labour this week.✦More frequent false contractions (Braxton Hicks).✦A stronger nesting instinct (bursts of energy, e.g. cleaning and tidying the house non-stop).✦Regular contractions starting, every 10 or 15 minutes.✦Regular contractions lasting longer.✦Contractions becoming more frequent and intense.✦Contractions getting stronger when you walk or lie down.✦Period-like pain in your back and lower belly.✦Diarrhoea.✦Blood-tinged mucus as the cervix softens and the mucus plug comes away (often called a 'show').✦Needing the toilet often.✦A small or large gush of amniotic fluid (waters breaking).
269: ✦If you have varicose veins, they may be more noticeable now.✦That's because progesterone relaxes your blood vessels.✦Your legs are also carrying more weight and more blood is circulating in your body.
270: ✦Right now you're focused on the birth and welcoming your baby, but soon you'll need to focus on breastfeeding.✦Your breast milk – with carbohydrates, proteins, fats (including long-chain fatty acids), prebiotics, vitamins, antibodies and nucleotides – will nourish your baby and adapt to their changing needs as they grow, supporting their development.
271: ✦You could give birth any moment now, so watch for signs of labour.✦These include your waters breaking, diarrhoea and nausea, a burst of energy, the mucus plug coming away and slightly bloody vaginal discharge.✦If you see blood in your discharge, labour may be 1–2 days away.✦But this isn't certain, so don't fixate on that timing.
272: ✦At this stage you probably feel so uncomfortable that you may think you never want to be pregnant again.✦But we suggest waiting until you hold your baby before making that decision.
273: ✦As a mother-to-be at this point, you may feel excited, distracted, anxious or even scared.✦You may be tense and overly sensitive.✦You may notice you're impatient and restless.✦All these emotional swings are completely normal.✦Go easy on yourself, relax and remember it will all be over very soon.
274: ✦You probably feel huge right now.✦Your uterus now fills your pelvis and most of your belly, and there's no room left to grow.✦So it sits under your ribs, and measurements hardly change from week to week.
275: ✦In the last month of pregnancy, nutrition is as important as ever.✦Keep eating a healthy, balanced diet and try not to gain much weight in the final week.✦Apart from your daily exercises, avoid activities that tire you.✦Travel isn't recommended in the final weeks of pregnancy.✦If you need to travel, talk to your doctor first.✦Take showers sitting down or with someone nearby.
276: ✦Some women prefer not to use medication for pain relief during labour.✦They choose to give birth as naturally as possible using different positions, massage, hypnotherapy, and breathing and relaxation techniques.✦These methods are usually taught in birth preparation classes.✦In the final weeks of pregnancy, relaxation techniques can help you stay calm.
277: ✦There's a very high chance of birth this week.✦A bloody, mucus-like discharge is an important sign that labour will start within 12–24 hours.✦The amniotic sac could rupture at any moment and your waters may break.✦There may be a lot of fluid or a little.✦Whatever the amount, if fluid leaks, contact your doctor right away.✦Pains that become stronger and unbearable are also signs that birth is near.✦In such cases, go to the hospital immediately.
278: ✦A pregnancy that goes past 40 weeks doesn't mean there's a problem.✦Almost half of all pregnancies go past 40 weeks.✦Some even last until 41 or 42 weeks.✦But your doctor won't let it go beyond 42 weeks.
279: ✦There's a very high chance of birth this week.✦A bloody, mucus-like discharge is an important sign that labour will start within 12–24 hours.✦The amniotic sac could rupture at any moment and your waters may break.✦There may be a lot of fluid or a little.✦Whatever the amount, if fluid leaks, contact your doctor right away.✦Pains that become stronger and unbearable are also signs that birth is near.✦In such cases, go to the hospital immediately.
280: ✦Newborns don't have as much blood on their skin as people think.✦For skin-to-skin contact after birth, the baby can be gently wiped with a towel and placed on the mother's chest.✦Delaying cord clamping by about a minute helps the baby part calmly from something familiar and helps prevent anaemia.✦Being placed on the mother right after birth lets the baby calm down to the sound of the mother's heartbeat.✦In recent years this has become common practice, recognising that before bathing or vaccines, the baby needs nothing more than the mother's arms.✦You can ask your doctor during pregnancy for skin-to-skin contact, now offered in many hospitals.✦It's very valuable for the baby to stay with the mother during and after the Apgar test.✦If there's no emergency, the baby should stay with the mother for the first 45 minutes to 1 hour.✦This way the baby feels safe, soothed by the parents' familiar voices and the feeling of being held (a natural incubator effect).✦Meeting this need for safety right after birth is said to help babies be calmer, including in infancy, and to trust life.✦If you request these practices in advance, you won't be disappointed after the birth.
